repositories.prompt_note: Use the ClawHub source tree and current main branch. Review every issue and PR with the same evidence standard. Propose auto-close for issues and pull requests that are certainly implemented on main; for pull requests only, also allow age-gated mostly implemented on main. Keep everything else open.

Use the ClawSweeper source tree and current main branch. Review bot automation, workflow, and documentation changes conservatively. Propose auto-close for issues and pull requests that are certainly implemented on main; for pull requests only, also allow age-gated mostly implemented on main. Keep everything else open for maintainer triage.

Use the OpenClaw Enterprise source tree and current main branch. Follow its AGENTS.md and authoritative platform design, verify implementation status before treating target-design capabilities as implemented, and preserve workspace, architecture, IAM, audit, persistence, and deployment boundaries. Require target-native integration evidence for platform behavior. Review only: keep issues and pull requests open for maintainer triage.

Use the openclaw-facetime source tree and current main branch. This is a macOS-native project: reviews touch SIP constraints, helper-process injection, Core Audio, and realtime capture paths, so weigh platform-specific evidence carefully and never assume Linux-runner reproduction proves or disproves macOS behavior. Propose auto-close only for issues and pull requests that are certainly implemented on main; keep anything platform-uncertain open for maintainer triage.

Use the fs-safe source tree and current main branch. Review filesystem-safety, path-handling, and package changes conservatively. Propose auto-close for issues and pull requests that are certainly implemented on main; for pull requests only, also allow age-gated mostly implemented on main. Keep everything else open for maintainer triage.

Use the Crabbox source tree and current default branch. Review its Go CLI, portable Node/PostgreSQL coordinator, Cloudflare coordinator, and documentation using target-native tooling and evidence. Propose auto-close for issues and pull requests that are certainly implemented on main; for pull requests only, also allow age-gated mostly implemented on main. Keep everything else open for maintainer triage.

Use the camsnap source tree and current main branch. Review camera discovery, RTSP/ONVIF behavior, Go changes, and cross-platform build behavior conservatively. Keep issues and pull requests open for maintainer triage.

Use the ShareX/ShareX source tree and current develop branch (ShareX uses develop as its active default branch, not main). Distinguish the two UI eras: ShareX 21.x and earlier used Windows Forms and GDI+ (Windows-only, legacy WinForms image editor), while ShareX 22.0 and later is the Avalonia UI rewrite (ShareX.Avalonia, ShareX.ImageEditor, ShareX.ScreenRecordingLib, ShareX.Platform.*). Check whether older WinForms or GDI+ issues still apply on current develop; when an old WinForms UI bug cannot be verified against Avalonia v22, keep it open as needs-info (unclear reproduction) asking whether it still reproduces on 22.4+, or propose stale_version_bug only with direct code evidence that the old component was replaced. For ShareX 22+ Avalonia regressions, check recent develop commits and open PRs closely. Never mention OpenClaw, docs.openclaw.ai, ClawHub, AI tools, or crustacean jokes. Never say or imply that ShareX is dropping, declining, or compromising Windows features because of cross-platform support or Avalonia. Write closeComment in plain American English, 2 to 5 short sentences, straight quotes, no em or en dashes, no headings or bullet lists, reading like a human ShareX maintainer. Review only: never auto-close directly.
